subject: VPC observability: evidence transport, collector ports, and retention agreement
messages:
From: Brian Cobb <brian.cobb@acmecloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security-team@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability plan for private VPC deployment — port mapping & retention

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security and ops teams want a short plan for how Redwood will ship logs/traces from the private VPC deployment into our SIEM. Key asks from Acme:

- Allowed outbound ports/protocols (we prefer HTTPS/HEC over raw syslog but need options)
- TLS termination & mutual TLS requirements
- Evidence retention window and on-disk encryption details
- Whether agents/collectors can be run in our subnet or need a managed forwarder

Can you send a recommended transport pattern and any sample config? I also attached the evidence matrix our auditors asked for.

Appreciate it,
Brian

--
Brian Cobb
Head of Platform Security, AcmeCloud
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Brian Cobb <brian.cobb@acmecloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability plan for private VPC deployment — port mapping & retention

Brian — thanks, and excellent list. High level recommendation below; attaching a one-page proposal (redwood-vpc-obsv-proposal-v1.pdf) and a populated example of Acme's evidence matrix.

Summary (recommended default):
- Transport: HTTPS to Splunk HEC endpoint (443) with optional fallback to TLS-wrapped syslog (6514) only if customer cannot provide HEC.
- Auth: mTLS for collector-to-Redwood-control-plane links; customer controls egress to their SIEM endpoint with HEC token for direct push.
- Collector placement: Prefer customer-run collector inside VPC (sidecar or central-forwarder) — reduces cross-tenant handling and simplifies egress auditing. Redwood can supply a lightweight forwarder image and Helm chart.
- Traces: OpenTelemetry (OTLP/gRPC) over 4317 with TLS. Traces should be sampled at source with Redwood's inline hooks for span correlation.
- Retention & encryption: Data in-transit encrypted with TLS 1.3; at-rest encryption for temporary buffers on the collector using customer-managed KMS where available. Retention on Redwood-managed artifacts is configurable; default handoff is immediate push to Acme SIEM (no long-term storage on Redwood).

Operational notes / Constraints:
- Ports: 443 (HEC), 6514 (syslog-TLS fallback), 4317 (OTLP/gRPC). If strict egress filtering is in place, only 443 is required with HEC-based ingestion.
- Evidence proofs: We provide signed delivery receipts and per-batch checksums in the metadata header so Acme can verify integrity after ingestion.

I've put a couple of action items below for alignment.

Attach: redwood-vpc-obsv-proposal-v1.pdf, acme-evidence-matrix.xlsx

Next steps / action items:
1) Acme to confirm allowed egress ports (443 and/or 4317/6514).
2) Redwood to produce sample Helm values for a forwarder and a reference OTLP pipeline.
3) Security sync to finalize mTLS certificate exchange process.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Brian Cobb <brian.cobb@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability plan for private VPC deployment — port mapping & retention

Looping in detailed compliance constraints from our side. A few clarifications we need before we lock the design:  

- For retention: if any buffered records are stored on Redwood-run infrastructure (e.g., during intermittent egress), the maximum buffer retention is 24 hours and data must be encrypted with CMK (customer-managed key). Confirm if Acme requires zero buffering on Redwood.
- SIEM formats: Splunk HEC: we can emit raw events or structured JSON with a metadata envelope; syslog fallback will be RFC5424. Which format does Acme expect for alerting pipelines?
- Audit logs: We will produce admin-level audit logs showing who pulled evidence bundles and when; to meet your auditors we need to know whether those logs should be pushed to your Splunk index or kept in a dedicated audit bucket.

If Acme prefers the push model (Redwood → your HEC), we will need an HEC token and a specific index target; if you prefer to pull (collector reads from local file), we'll provide signed manifests for verification.

Marissa — can you call out the tracehook details (span correlation keys and OTLP attributes) in the same doc?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Brian Cobb <brian.cobb@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 20:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability plan for private VPC deployment — port mapping & retention

Brian / team — quick follow-up on tracing and correlation:  

- Trace transport: OTLP/gRPC to your OTLP collector (port 4317) with TLS. If you cannot open 4317 outbound, OTLP/HTTP (4318) is acceptable but less efficient for high-throughput traces.
- Span correlation: We add two custom attributes to each span: redwood.request_id and redwood.instance_id. We also inject a customer_id tag equal to AcmeCloud for cross-index joins.
- Sampling: Default sample rate is 0.5% for production; we recommend a 3-tier policy: baseline (0.5%), spike-capture (10% for error traces), and config-driven full trace for canaries.

For acceptance testing we will provide a small test suite that generates synthetic traces and verifies OTLP ingestion and tag presence. I've dropped the test suite and a minimal Helm values snippet into the shared Drive link.

If this matches your requirements, we'll update the proposal PDF with the exact HEC header samples and certificate exchange steps.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Observability, Redwood Inference
